publicDeclarationReviews.name: Shao.C2.IntervalSineCosineSeries.integerCosineTerm_neg
publicDeclarationReviews.reason: The integer cast of -n is the real negative; its square is unchanged. The phase is the negative of the original phase and cos is even. No positivity assumption is needed.

publicDeclarationReviews.name: Shao.C2.IntervalSineCosineSeries.integerCosineTerm_pos_summable
publicDeclarationReviews.reason: Use the qualified weightedGaussian summability theorem with c=pi^2/8>0, x=T/a^2>0, r=0. The complete real norm is at most the positive exponential because |cos|<=1; cast normalization and nonzero a make its exponent exactly the Gaussian exponent.

publicDeclarationReviews.name: Shao.C2.IntervalSineCosineSeries.integerCosineTerm_hasSum
publicDeclarationReviews.reason: The positive modes have sum S. zero_add inserts precisely the n=0 mode into the nonnegative integer sequence. Whole-function evenness identifies the strictly negative sequence -(n+1) with the positive one. The disjoint exhaustive natural/negative-natural integer decomposition gives f(0)+S+S. f(0)=1 and the explicit scalar equality yield 1+2S.

publicDeclarationReviews.name: Shao.C2.IntervalSineCosineSeries.integerCosineTerm_summable
publicDeclarationReviews.reason: This is the genuine existence of a real unconditional integer sum, obtained from the immediately preceding HasSum witness, not an equality of fallback tsum values.

publicDeclarationReviews.name: Shao.C2.IntervalSineCosineSeries.sineTerm_cosine_difference
publicDeclarationReviews.reason: Write k=n+1 and frequency=k*pi/(2a). The exponential is exp(-frequency^2*T/2). The first phase is -(frequency*(y+a)-frequency*(z+a)); the second is their sum. cos_sub minus cos_add is 2*sin(A)*sin(B). Multiplying by exp/(2a) recovers the literal 1/a-normalized sineTerm. a>0 pays every denominator; T,y,z are otherwise unrestricted.

publicDeclarationReviews.name: Shao.C2.IntervalSineCosineSeries.sineSeries_eq_integer_cosine
publicDeclarationReviews.reason: The two positive-mode functions are genuinely summable. HasSum.sub then mul_left supplies their scaled difference sum. Unfolding mixedSineTerm at (0,0), with iteratedDeriv_zero twice, gives the term identity on the complete natural-index function. Both full integer sums equal 1+2 times their positive sums; their zero modes cancel. Exact scalar algebra yields the coefficient 1/(4a).

originalSource.scopeAttribution: Auxiliary integer-cosine conversion for the analytic sine series. The original lines invoke the killed-kernel sine expansion, but do not literally display the present conversion identity. Attribution-only erratum accepted; original receipt and release untouched.

acceptedScope: For a>0,T>0 and arbitrary real z,y: genuine positive and full-integer cosine summability, exact evenness and zero-mode account, termwise sine/cosine identity retaining z+y+2a, and mixedSineSeries 0 0 = (wholeIntegerCosine(z-y)-wholeIntegerCosine(z+y+2a))/(4a).
boundaryChecks: Positive/full-integer summability uses T>0 and a>0; no T=0 fallback-sum claim.
Evenness is unconditional in a,T,u,n; the pointwise sine identity needs only a>0, with arbitrary T,y,z.
Natural index n denotes strictly positive mode n+1, including first mode 1. The integer zero mode is exactly 1 and cancels between the two full sums.
The reflected phase is z+y+2a. At a wall this preserves the correct shifted/parity behavior; no unshifted cosine replacement was made.
No interior-domain hypothesis was silently added: the analytic identity is valid for arbitrary real endpoints.
